Cloudflare zone policy

The adjacent zone-policy.json is the desired state for the eaglepass.io minimum TLS version. Owner approved minimum TLS 1.2 on November 3, 2026 under maintenance Issue 103. Seven complete UTC days of prior analytics reported no TLS 1.0/1.1 HTTPS requests; this does not prove an exhaustive dormant-client inventory. TLS 1.0/1.1 clients will be rejected.

Ownership and scoped application

No existing Terraform resource owns this zone setting. Use the existing authorized Cloudflare provider connection and its zone-settings API workflow for this one declared setting. This does not authorize a broad external Terraform apply, provider migration, credential change or permission grant. Cloudflare DNS, tunnel, access and existing Terraform state remain unchanged.

  1. Validate the JSON and review its exact desired value, target and rollback. Commit and push the desired state to canonical Gitea master before application.
  2. Read the exact zone and confirm name/account identity. Read minimum TLS, SSL mode, browser checking and security level. Require editable minimum TLS; initial application expects 1.0 and preserved fields as declared. If already 1.2, verify rather than reapply. Stop on other drift or permission denial.
  3. Construct the exact provider request from the published JSON: PATCH /zones/{zone_id}/settings/min_tls_version with body containing only value=settings.min_tls_version. No other setting may be written.
  4. Require provider success and fresh GET readback of 1.2. Verify every preserve field unchanged. Verify public TLS 1.2/1.3 handshakes and application health. Confirm TLS 1.0/1.1 protocol rejection from a capable client; distinguish local client limitations from server rejection.
  5. Retain sanitized source-bound application/verification evidence and update Issue 103. Never retain credentials or visitor records.

Rollback

If this policy causes a required-client regression, first revert desired minimum to the recorded rollback value 1.0 in Git, validate, commit and push. Apply only the same minimum-TLS endpoint, then verify readback and preserved fields. Do not weaken strict SSL or alter access policy as a workaround.

Prior aggregate evidence. NAS restrictions and protected Zot remain unaffected.
